narrative.overview:
The system pairs the authority of a printed reference atlas with the immediacy of a living climate record. A framed, full-viewport filmic hero establishes scale and urgency; everything below it becomes quieter, flatter, and more exact so the data can carry the argument.

IBM Plex gives the experience a direct editorial voice without losing technical credibility. Strong headlines, compact labels, mono numerals, generous chapter spacing, and bounded analytical stages create a clear reading rhythm. Light mode feels like warm paper and ink; dark mode feels like graphite and illuminated plotting marks.
keyCharacteristics: Immersive framed motion at the opening, followed by restrained analytical chapters.
Bottom-anchored editorial composition with a split headline and supporting column.
Warm paper light surfaces and near-black graphite dark surfaces.
Blue, orange, and green country series that stay synchronized across every view.
Flat, bordered controls and plot stages with generous whitespace between chapters.
Compact labels and monospaced, tabular numerals for fast data scanning.

rules.name: The Three-Country Rule
rules.body: Blue is always country one, orange country two, and green country three. Never reorder or repurpose these hues within a view.

rules.name: The Quiet Field Rule
rules.body: Use neutral surfaces and hairlines for structure. Saturated color must encode action, selection, magnitude, or focus.

rules.name: The Theme Pair Rule
rules.body: Light and dark modes preserve semantic roles and relative contrast; they do not introduce a separate brand palette.

rules.name: The Data Has a Different Voice Rule
rules.body: Use IBM Plex Mono only for years, measures, and compact technical metadata; prose and navigation stay in IBM Plex Sans.

rules.name: The Tight Headline Rule
rules.body: Large editorial headings use heavy weight, compact line height, and negative tracking. Do not imitate their density in body copy.

rules.name: The Open Chapter Rule
rules.body: Section spacing and hairlines define the story. Use cards for controls, tables, and plots, not as a wrapper around every chapter.

rules.name: The Pinned Context Rule
rules.body: When a data region must scroll horizontally, keep the identifying label visible and provide a plain-language scroll hint on small screens.

rules.name: The Cinematic Exception Rule
rules.body: Ambient shadow belongs to the hero and its over-video actions. Analytical surfaces use tone and borders instead.

rules.name: The Nested Radius Rule
rules.body: Larger outer surfaces receive the larger radius. Inner controls step down in radius so layers remain visually ordered.

dos: Do keep Explore the atlas as the primary action before Donate.
Do preserve blue, orange, and green slot order in controls, tables, bubbles, and trend lines.
Do use warm paper and graphite surface stacks with one-pixel hairlines for analytical structure.
Do pair monospaced tabular numerals with plain-language labels and notes.
Do maintain open chapter spacing, bounded controls, and bounded plot stages at every viewport.
Do keep mobile maps legible and comparison tables horizontally scrollable with the country column pinned.
Do disable motion and the hero video when reduced motion is requested.
donts: Don't use decorative color where it could be mistaken for a series, selection, magnitude, or focus state.
Don't add ambient shadows to analytical cards, tables, toolbars, or chart stages.
Don't wrap every chapter in a card or compress the whitespace that separates the analytical story.
Don't change a country's assigned hue between views or rely on color without a nearby country name.
Don't let large chart canvases force the mobile page wider than the viewport.
Don't use the hero's cinematic motion language inside the analytical chapters.
